assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is document scoring, ranking, and relevance optimization within IR, finer than a whole-IR KB
evaluation is graded-relevance centric (nDCG/ERR) unless a project overrides the grade scale
a candidate document set is already retrieved; first-stage recall/indexing is out of scope
exclusions: query understanding/NLU beyond intent classes used for relevance
dense retrieval/embedding model training internals (referenced only as hybrid signal)
privacy and security controls beyond fairness exposure

competency_questions.question: What relevance notion (binary vs graded, topical vs intent) does the ranking system optimize?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REL_MODEL defines scale and intent classes

competency_questions.question: How is ranking quality measured for graded relevance and what cutoff applies?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVAL_NDCG_ERR + REL_MODEL define metric and grades

competency_questions.question: What lexical baseline scorer is used and how does it weight terms?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TFIDF and BM25_CORE define term weighting

competency_questions.question: How are BM25 tf-saturation, length normalization, and field weights configured?
How are scoring/smoothing hyperparameters tuned without overfitting small judged sets?
How does the language-model approach score documents and handle zero probabilities?
How are term proximity and term dependence incorporated into scoring?
How is the query reformulated via explicit or pseudo relevance feedback and how is drift controlled?
What features and LTR objective drive the learned ranker and how is leakage prevented?
How is a learned ranker trained and validated against the target ranking metric?
How are click logs debiased for position bias before being used as relevance signals?
How is result diversity/novelty achieved for ambiguous queries?
How is exposure fairness enforced while preserving ranking utility?
How are offline metric gains reconciled with online A/B before promotion?

glossary.definition: degree a document satisfies a query's information need under the chosen grade scale
diminishing contribution of additional term occurrences controlled by BM25 k1
adjustment of scores for document length controlled by BM25 b
interpolation of document and collection language models to avoid zero probabilities
supervised learning of a ranking function from labeled query-document features
tendency of users to click higher-ranked results irrespective of relevance
normalized discounted cumulative gain, a graded position-discounted ranking metric
re-ranking to cover multiple query aspects and reduce redundancy
distribution of result exposure across protected groups within a utility budget

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for ranking and relevance work units in absence of supplied datasets

nodes.definition: Define the relevance notion (topical, binary vs graded, query intent) that all ranking objectives optimize toward.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: judgment guidelines revised or intent taxonomy changes

pros.claim: Anchors every downstream metric and scorer to a single relevance definition
pros.example: graded 0-4 scale shared by nDCG and LTR labels

cons.claim: Wrong relevance definition silently invalidates all downstream evaluation
cons.example: binary labels hide ordering quality needed for nDCG

acceptance_tests: relevance scale documented with examples per grade
intent classes enumerated and mutually exclusive
revisit_triggers: metric disagreement traced to label semantics

nodes.definition: Compute classic term-frequency times inverse-document-frequency weights as a baseline bag-of-words scorer.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: baseline replaced by bm25 as default scorer

pros.claim: Cheap interpretable baseline that exposes term-weighting intuition
pros.example: idf downweights stopwords without a stoplist

cons.claim: Unbounded tf and no length normalization overweights long/repetitive docs
cons.example: 100-mention spam doc beats concise relevant doc

nodes.definition: Score documents with Okapi BM25 combining saturating tf, idf, and length normalization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: lexical scorer swapped or hybridized with dense retrieval

pros.claim: Strong robust lexical baseline that is hard to beat on many corpora
pros.example: BM25 default in Lucene/Elasticsearch

cons.claim: Vocabulary mismatch unaddressed without expansion or dense signals
cons.example: query 'car' misses doc saying 'automobile'

acceptance_tests: scores reproduce reference BM25 on a fixed fixture

nodes.definition: Tune BM25 k1 controlling term-frequency saturation curvature for the target corpus.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: corpus term-frequency distribution changes materially

pros.claim: Adapts repetition handling to corpus verbosity
pros.example: lower k1 for terse logs, higher for prose

cons.claim: Overfit k1 on small judged sets generalizes poorly
cons.example: k1 tuned on 30 queries fails on full traffic

failure_modes: entangling k1 with b during sweep

nodes.definition: Tune BM25 b controlling document-length normalization strength against length bias.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: document length distribution shifts

pros.claim: Removes systematic favoring of long documents
pros.example: b near 1 fully normalizes verbose corpora

cons.claim: Over-normalization penalizes legitimately long authoritative docs
cons.example: b=1 hurts long manuals that are truly relevant

failure_modes: tuning b without holding k1 fixed

nodes.definition: Combine per-field BM25 contributions (title, body, anchors) with field weights and per-field length norms.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: document field schema changes (new field or removed field)

pros.claim: Exploits structure so title matches outrank incidental body matches
pros.example: title weight 3x body lifts navigational queries

cons.claim: Field weight space expands tuning surface and overfit risk
cons.example: per-field weights overfit when fields sparse

failure_modes: combining fields after saturation instead of before

nodes.definition: Rank documents by probability that the document language model generates the query.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: switch from heuristic weighting to generative LM scoring

pros.claim: Principled probabilistic ranking with clean smoothing theory
pros.example: unifies scoring and smoothing under one model

cons.claim: Requires smoothing to handle zero probabilities; sensitive to it
cons.example: unsmoothed zero-prob term zeroes the whole doc score

nodes.definition: Apply Dirichlet or Jelinek-Mercer smoothing to interpolate document and collection language models.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: query length distribution or collection statistics change

pros.claim: Dirichlet smoothing adapts to doc length; JM gives idf-like effect
pros.example: mu~2000 robust default across TREC collections

cons.claim: Wrong smoothing parameter degrades short vs long query performance
cons.example: fixed lambda hurts verbose queries

failure_modes: length-insensitive smoothing on mixed query lengths

nodes.definition: Boost documents where query terms appear close together using proximity and term-dependence (MRF/sequential dependence) features.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: phrase-heavy or entity queries increase in traffic

pros.claim: Captures phrase intent missed by independent term scoring
pros.example: 'new york' near-match beats scattered 'new'+'york'

cons.claim: Position indexing and windowing add cost and tuning complexity
cons.example: sequential dependence triples feature cost

nodes.definition: Reformulate the query vector toward judged-relevant and away from non-relevant documents via Rocchio.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: explicit judgment availability changes

pros.claim: Large recall gains when explicit judgments exist
pros.example: adding relevant-doc terms recovers synonyms

cons.claim: Requires user judgments rarely available at scale
cons.example: explicit feedback absent in web search

nodes.definition: Assume top-k initially retrieved documents are relevant and expand the query from their terms without explicit judgments.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: first-pass precision@k drops, threatening expansion quality

pros.claim: Recall gains with no human labels needed
pros.example: RM3 lifts ad-hoc retrieval on TREC

cons.claim: Query drift when top-k are off-topic amplifies errors
cons.example: ambiguous query expands into wrong sense

failure_modes: expansion on too few pseudo-relevant docs

nodes.definition: Engineer query, document, and query-document features (BM25, proximity, freshness, quality) as inputs to learning-to-rank.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new signal source added or feature drift detected

pros.claim: Feature quality dominates LTR gains more than model class
pros.example: adding freshness feature fixes news queries

cons.claim: Train-serve skew and leakage silently inflate offline metrics
cons.example: label-derived feature leaks future clicks

acceptance_tests: no feature derived from the label
train and serve feature parity test passes

nodes.definition: Choose the learning-to-rank objective family (pointwise regression, pairwise preference, listwise) matched to the evaluation metric.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: target evaluation metric changes

pros.claim: Listwise objectives directly optimize ranking metrics
pros.example: listwise aligns loss with nDCG ordering

cons.claim: Pointwise ignores relative order; mismatched loss caps quality
cons.example: regressing grades ignores top-rank emphasis

nodes.definition: Train a LambdaMART gradient-boosted tree ranker using nDCG-weighted pairwise lambda gradients.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: feature set or label distribution changes materially

pros.claim: Strong tabular ranker dominating many LTR benchmarks
pros.example: LambdaMART tops MSLR/Yahoo LTR

cons.claim: Opaque, overfits noisy labels, needs regularization and monitoring
cons.example: deep trees memorize click noise

failure_modes: metric-train mismatch (delta nDCG vs deployed metric)
acceptance_tests: offline nDCG gain holds on held-out queries
no single feature dominates via importance audit

nodes.definition: Model user clicks (cascade, DBN, PBM) to debias implicit feedback and estimate relevance from logs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: UI layout change alters examination/position bias

pros.claim: Turns abundant logs into relevance labels at scale
pros.example: PBM separates examination from relevance

cons.claim: Position and presentation bias corrupt naive CTR labels
cons.example: top result clicked more regardless of relevance

failure_modes: ignoring position bias yields biased labels
acceptance_tests: estimated relevance correlates with held-out judgments

nodes.definition: Apply inverse-propensity-scoring to train and evaluate rankers from biased click logs without bias-confounded estimates.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logging policy changes, invalidating propensities

pros.claim: Unbiased gradient/estimate under correct propensities
pros.example: IPS recovers true ranker offline

cons.claim: High variance and wrong propensities silently bias results
cons.example: tiny propensities explode weights

acceptance_tests: IPS estimate matches online A/B within CI

nodes.definition: Re-rank for result diversity and novelty using MMR / intent-aware diversification to cover query aspects.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ambiguous-query share increases

pros.claim: Covers multiple intents for ambiguous queries
pros.example: 'jaguar' shows car and animal results

cons.claim: Trades top-1 relevance for coverage; lambda mistuning hurts
cons.example: over-diversifying pushes best result down

nodes.definition: Constrain or post-process rankings for exposure fairness across protected groups while preserving utility.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: fairness policy or protected-group definition changes

pros.claim: Mitigates winner-take-all exposure harms
pros.example: equal-exposure constraint balances providers

cons.claim: Constraints reduce utility and can mis-specify protected groups
cons.example: wrong group proxy creates new harm

nodes.definition: Evaluate rankings with graded metrics nDCG and ERR, including gain/discount and cutoff choices.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: relevance grade scale or cutoff policy changes

pros.claim: Graded position-discounted metrics reward top-rank quality
pros.example: nDCG@10 standard for graded ad-hoc eval

cons.claim: Metric/cutoff choice changes conclusions; small samples noisy
cons.example: nDCG@3 vs @10 flip system ranking

acceptance_tests: ideal ranking computed from full judged set

nodes.definition: Reconcile offline metric gains with online A/B outcomes before promoting a ranking change to production.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: offline-online divergence observed on a launch

pros.claim: Prevents shipping offline-only wins that regress users
pros.example: interleaving catches nDCG win that drops CTR

cons.claim: Online tests are slow, costly, and confounded by seasonality
cons.example: two-week A/B delays every ranking change

acceptance_tests: online result agrees in sign with offline before promotion

edges.why_related: tf-idf scores must target the chosen relevance notion
edges.benefit_of_coupling: grounds baseline in a real objective
edges.risk_of_conflict: baseline optimizes a stale relevance idea
edges.example: binary vs graded changes scorer fit
edges.resolution_rule: relevance definition dominates; refit baseline if it changes

edges.why_related: bm25 ranking targets the defined relevance notion
edges.resolution_rule: relevance definition dominates

edges.why_related: bm25 generalizes tf-idf with saturation and length norm
edges.resolution_rule: establish tf-idf baseline before bm25 comparison

edges.why_related: k1 tuning requires a working bm25 scorer
edges.resolution_rule: fix scorer correctness before tuning k1

edges.why_related: b tuning requires a working bm25 scorer
edges.resolution_rule: fix scorer correctness before tuning b

edges.why_related: k1 and b interact; tuning one shifts the other's optimum
edges.benefit_of_coupling: joint tuning finds better operating point
edges.resolution_rule: grid/joint search dominates; never tune one with the other unfixed

edges.why_related: BM25F extends bm25 to structured fields
edges.resolution_rule: validate single-field bm25 before field weighting

edges.why_related: per-field k1 bounds BM25F field saturation
edges.resolution_rule: reuse tuned k1 as per-field prior; re-tune only if field stats differ

edges.why_related: per-field length norm bounds BM25F
edges.resolution_rule: reuse tuned b as per-field prior

edges.why_related: query-likelihood ranking targets the relevance notion
edges.resolution_rule: relevance definition dominates

edges.why_related: smoothing is required to make query-likelihood usable
edges.resolution_rule: apply smoothing before using LM scores

edges.why_related: both are bag-of-words term-distribution scorers
edges.resolution_rule: treat as distinct families; keep separate nodes

edges.why_related: proximity features augment a lexical base score
edges.resolution_rule: stabilize base scorer before adding dependence features

edges.why_related: feedback reweights query toward defined relevance
edges.resolution_rule: relevance definition dominates expansion target

edges.why_related: rocchio operates on tf-idf vectors
edges.resolution_rule: build vectors before reweighting

edges.why_related: pseudo-relevance feedback adapts rocchio without judgments
edges.resolution_rule: derive PRF settings from feedback theory, retune weights

edges.why_related: RM3-style PRF builds on LM scoring
edges.resolution_rule: LM smoothing settled before PRF interpolation

edges.why_related: PRF second pass can revisit base ranking quality
edges.resolution_rule: stop after one expansion round unless precision@k improves; max 2 rounds

edges.why_related: bm25 score is a core LTR feature
edges.resolution_rule: compute base scores before feature assembly

edges.why_related: proximity features feed LTR
edges.resolution_rule: include dependence features in schema

edges.why_related: labels must match relevance definition to avoid leakage
edges.resolution_rule: forbid label-derived features

edges.why_related: objective choice consumes the feature set
edges.benefit_of_coupling: matches loss to features and metric
edges.resolution_rule: finalize feature schema before objective

edges.why_related: objective must align with the relevance metric
edges.resolution_rule: align loss with eval metric

edges.why_related: LambdaMART instantiates a listwise/pairwise objective
edges.resolution_rule: fix objective before training ranker

edges.why_related: the ranker trains on the engineered features
edges.resolution_rule: resolve leakage and skew before training

edges.why_related: the eval metric constrains the objective family
edges.resolution_rule: metric definition bounds objective choice

edges.why_related: click models estimate the defined relevance from logs
edges.resolution_rule: relevance definition dominates target of estimation

edges.why_related: propensities for IPS come from the click/examination model
edges.resolution_rule: estimate propensities before IPS weighting

edges.why_related: debiased click relevance becomes training labels/features
edges.resolution_rule: use debiased estimates only; audit bias

edges.why_related: IPS weighting changes the ranker's training distribution
edges.resolution_rule: clip propensities; validate against online before trust

edges.why_related: MMR re-ranks an existing relevance ranking
edges.resolution_rule: produce base ranking before diversification

edges.why_related: relevance definition bounds acceptable diversity loss
edges.resolution_rule: relevance floor constrains diversity

edges.why_related: diversity and fairness re-ranking compete for the same slots
edges.benefit_of_coupling: one re-rank stage can serve both
edges.resolution_rule: define a single re-rank objective with explicit weights; human review on conflict

edges.why_related: graded metrics consume the relevance grade scale
edges.resolution_rule: grade scale fixed before metric computation

edges.why_related: offline metric results trigger ranker retraining
edges.resolution_rule: retrain only on material delta>=0.01 nDCG; max 3 cycles

edges.why_related: a trained ranker is the candidate for online validation
edges.resolution_rule: offline gain required before online test

edges.why_related: unbiased offline estimates feed the promotion gate
edges.resolution_rule: use debiased estimate at the gate

edges.why_related: offline metric report is an input to promotion
edges.resolution_rule: require online agreement before promote

edges.why_related: fairness audit bounds what may be promoted
edges.resolution_rule: fairness guardrail must pass before promotion

conflict_axes.trigger: query expansion adds terms that raise recall but inject off-topic drift
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if precision@k drops below baseline, precision side dominates and expansion is reduced
conflict_axes.example: ambiguous query 'jaguar' PRF drifts to cars, recall up precision down

conflict_axes.trigger: diversification displaces the most relevant result to cover more aspects
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: relevance floor dominates; diversity may not push top result below floor
conflict_axes.example: MMR lambda too low buries best answer for variety

conflict_axes.trigger: fairness exposure constraints reduce utility-optimal ordering
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: policy-mandated fairness dominates within an agreed utility-loss budget; beyond budget escalate
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: utility loss exceeds agreed budget or protected group proxy uncertain
conflict_axes.example: equal-exposure constraint demotes most relevant provider

conflict_axes.trigger: two re-ranking objectives compete for the same result slots
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: a single combined re-rank objective dominates stacked independent re-rankers
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: stacked re-rankers oscillate or both metrics regress
conflict_axes.example: MMR then fairness re-rank undo each other

conflict_axes.trigger: offline nDCG improves but online A/B shows neutral or negative user impact
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: online outcome dominates offline gain for promotion decisions
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: offline and online disagree in sign
conflict_axes.example: nDCG win that lowers session success

conflict_axes.trigger: low propensities make IPS unbiased but high-variance and unstable to train on
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: variance control via clipping dominates pure unbiasedness when estimates are unstable
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: effective sample size collapses or weights explode

conflict_axes.trigger: hyperparameters tuned on a small judged set overfit and fail on full traffic
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: held-out generalization dominates in-sample metric maximization
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: held-out metric drops while in-sample rises
conflict_axes.example: k1 tuned on 30 queries regresses on full set

conflict_axes.trigger: strict lexical matching misses synonyms while expansion/dependence risk noise
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: add semantic/expansion signal only when measured vocabulary mismatch justifies the added noise
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: expansion increases noise faster than recall

edge_cases.example: freshness feature points to deprecated source

edge_cases.failure_mode: expansion drifts query to wrong sense

joint grid search vs sequential comparison

edge_cases.failure_mode: train-eval metric mismatch flips system ranking
edge_cases.detection_method: compare loss cutoff to report cutoff

edge_cases.example: rare query term absent in doc collapses score
edge_cases.detection_method: check for zero-score documents with partial matches

edge_cases.failure_mode: overfit params regress on full traffic

audit group assignment accuracy and exposure deltas

edge_cases.example: new intent class not in grade scale
edge_cases.detection_method: version check between grade scale and metric config

workflow.objective: fix relevance definition, grade scale, and intent classes
acceptance_tests: grade scale has examples per grade
workflow.do_first_because: all scorers and metrics depend on a stable relevance definition

workflow.objective: define nDCG/ERR metric, gain, discount, and cutoff before tuning
workflow.do_first_because: tuning and objective choice must target a fixed metric to avoid rework

workflow.objective: stand up tf-idf and BM25 baseline scorers
workflow.do_first_because: a correct baseline is the comparison anchor for all later gains

workflow.objective: jointly tune k1, b and field weights on held-out queries
acceptance_tests: held-out metric not worse than in-sample default
workflow.do_first_because: k1/b interact; joint tuning before downstream features prevents re-tuning churn

workflow.objective: add LM scoring with smoothing and proximity/dependence features
acceptance_tests: no zero-score docs with partial matches
workflow.do_first_because: these alternative/augmenting scorers are cheaper to validate before learned ranking

workflow.objective: add relevance and pseudo-relevance feedback with drift controls
workflow.do_first_because: expansion can drift; validate precision before feeding learned ranking

workflow.objective: build click model and IPS debiasing for log-derived labels
acceptance_tests: debiased labels correlate with held-out judgments
workflow.do_first_because: learned ranker quality depends on unbiased labels; debias before training

workflow.objective: engineer features and choose metric-aligned LTR objective
entry_criteria: base scores, proximity, debiased labels ready
workflow.do_first_because: feature integrity and metric-aligned objective prevent inflated offline wins

workflow.objective: train LambdaMART ranker and produce offline metric report
acceptance_tests: offline nDCG gain holds on held-out queries
workflow.do_first_because: training depends on stable validated features and objective

workflow.objective: apply unified diversity+fairness re-ranking with utility floor
workflow.do_first_because: fairness and diversity compete; resolve as one objective with human review before lock

workflow.objective: reconcile offline gains with online A/B and gate promotion
workflow.do_first_because: irreversible production launch must pass online validation and human review last

dominance_rules.trigger: offline gain conflicts with online or guardrail outcome
dominance_rules.rule: online A/B and guardrails dominate offline metric for promotion
dominance_rules.required_action: block promotion until online sign agreement
dominance_rules.example: nDCG win that lowers session success is not shipped

dominance_rules.trigger: dependency order conflicts with value-first ordering
dominance_rules.rule: true prerequisites are sequenced before higher-value-but-dependent work
dominance_rules.required_action: sequence REL_MODEL and EVAL before scorers/LTR
dominance_rules.example: do not train LambdaMART before features validated

dominance_rules.rule: evidence labels and grounding dominate apparent numeric precision
dominance_rules.example: no observed label without observed data

dominance_rules.trigger: hard lock requested before QA passes
dominance_rules.rule: QA, acceptance tests, and validation dominate any lock request
dominance_rules.required_action: run acceptance tests before any lock escalation
dominance_rules.example: no hard lock before online validation

dominance_rules.trigger: automation would make an irreversible or high-risk ranking decision
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for fairness, promotion, and irreversible launches
dominance_rules.example: fairness intervention and promotion require human sign-off

dominance_rules.trigger: label-derived or leaky feature improves offline metric
dominance_rules.rule: feature/label integrity dominates offline metric gains
dominance_rules.example: leakage test blocks the inflated win

dominance_rules.trigger: diversity and fairness re-rankers conflict for slots
dominance_rules.rule: a single combined re-rank objective dominates independent stacked re-rankers
dominance_rules.example: stop stacking MMR then fairness re-rank

dominance_rules.trigger: IPS unbiasedness produces unstable high-variance training
dominance_rules.rule: variance control dominates when propensity estimates are unstable
dominance_rules.example: clip propensity floor to bound weights

dominance_rules.trigger: in-sample tuning gain conflicts with held-out generalization
diversity pushes top relevant result below relevance floor
dominance_rules.rule: relevance floor dominates diversity coverage at the top
dominance_rules.required_action: cap MMR displacement above the floor
dominance_rules.example: best answer must stay in top positions

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix relevance definition before any scorer or metric work
anti_rework_rules.rationale: all downstream targets depend on the relevance notion
anti_rework_rules.example: building BM25 before grade scale exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the evaluation metric before tuning or objective selection
anti_rework_rules.rationale: tuning to a moving metric forces re-tuning
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: params tuned then metric cutoff changes
anti_rework_rules.example: tuning k1 before nDCG cutoff fixed

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate baseline scorer before tuning hyperparameters
anti_rework_rules.rationale: tuning a broken scorer wastes effort
anti_rework_rules.example: sweeping b on an incorrect scorer

anti_rework_rules.rule: jointly tune k1 and b, never independently
anti_rework_rules.rationale: k1/b interaction makes sequential tuning suboptimal
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: one tuned while the other floats

anti_rework_rules.rule: apply smoothing before using language-model scores
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: LM scores with zeros on partial matches

anti_rework_rules.rule: debias click logs before using them as labels
anti_rework_rules.rationale: biased labels corrupt every learned ranker

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve feature leakage and skew before training the ranker
anti_rework_rules.rationale: leaky features inflate offline metrics and ship regressions

anti_rework_rules.rule: finalize feature schema and objective before training
anti_rework_rules.example: retrain churn from late feature edits

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve diversity vs fairness as one objective before re-rank lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: stacked re-rankers oscillate and double rework

anti_rework_rules.rule: require online validation before promoting any ranking change
